features.title: Identify the earliest publicly available Minecraft reference
features.body: Verify the May 2009 release chronology, including 0.0.10a and 0.0.11a. Distinguish original public availability, playability and the provenance of surviving artifacts. Recommend the earliest sufficiently documented reference and record uncertainties.

features.title: Document sources and observed historical behavior
features.body: Record dated evidence for controls, behavior, constraints and reported bugs. Mark confidence, conflicts, artifact provenance and any rights restrictions. Keep reference binaries and code outside Git.

features.title: Define the first Craft++ feature scope
features.body: After the reference decision, document genre-level capabilities in scope, explicit exclusions, original design choices and observable acceptance criteria. Record how historical quirks inform design decisions.

features.title: Specify the C++ toolchain and repository layout
features.body: Document the Visual Studio 2026 MSVC toolset, Windows SDK, C++ standard, source layout and path to later Linux support.

features.title: Evaluate rendering backends, including Vulkan
features.body: Compare Vulkan and credible alternatives on Windows and Linux support, portability, debugging, driver coverage and implementation cost. Record the decision and the profiling evidence needed to validate assumptions.

features.title: Set up a reproducible Visual Studio and MSBuild build
features.body: Add a native Visual Studio solution with a Windows x64 world library. Verify Debug and Release builds and document how to open and build the solution.

features.title: Prepare the first historically informed implementation
features.body: After the reference, feature scope and technical decisions are recorded, define a small implementation sequence and acceptance checks for original Craft++ gameplay and assets. Document the first actionable slice.
